=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- workflow-templates/.claude/scripts/escalation_ledger.py:93, 99, 228 | severity=NIT | confidence=[4]
  PROBLEM: The date is validated with a regex that accepts syntactically-shaped but semantically-impossible dates (e.g. `2026-13-45`, `2026-02-30`, `2026-04-31`, `0000-00-00`). Two paths accept these: `record` checks `--date` against DATE_RE, and `parse_entries` matches log lines against ENTRY_RE's inline date pattern (around line 99).
  WHY: The script's contract is to validate the date, but the regex does not. An invalid date written by `record` would be accepted back by `parse_entries` and persist in the log across sessions. The fingerprint does not include the date so collisions are not a concern, but a corrupted log date silently passes the validator and would be surfaced as a malformed `## Escalations` line only if a future maintainer tightens the parser.
- TASK_GAP
  Requirement: "Each cap counts one extra round per `ES-<n>` entry with `choice=budget` or `choice=descope` for the same stop id (for `intervention-cap`, only entries whose `why=` names the same PR); a repeat stop goes back to the judge, where the same fingerprint gets only unused choices."
  Expected change site: workflow-templates/.claude/commands/implement-plan-claude.md, the cap bullets in steps 7, 8, 9, 10, 12.
  Evidence of absence: lines 81 and 89 say "plus any the [escalation judge] granted" but do not name the stop id, so a future cap added to the file could miss the matching rule. The `intervention-cap` "same PR" qualifier lives in the Escalations section prose (around line 308) but is not surfaced into the cap bullets themselves. No contract test pins the cap-counting semantics, so a future change that drops the "same PR" qualifier or the "per stop id" matching would not be caught.
  SEVERITY: NIT
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 2
- TASK_GAP
  Requirement: "The judge's `descope` choice for `intervention-cap` is a single `[claude-intervention] descope ES-<n>` commit on the blocked PR's own branch; for other stops it is a new revert PR from `claude/implement-plan-<slug>-descope-<n>`."
  Expected change site: workflow-templates/.claude/commands/escalation-judge.md step 8 hand-on, and the `Escalation:` resume line template in workflow-templates/.claude/commands/implement-plan-claude.md.
  Evidence of absence: The `Escalation: ES-<n> <budget | descope> — <the narrower fix | the de-scoped part>` line (implement-plan-claude.md around line 137) does not carry the original stop id, and step 8's hand-on text only names `<next stage>` as `descope ES-<n>` without the stop id. The `descope ES-<n>` stage therefore cannot tell from the resume block alone whether to commit on the blocked PR's branch or open a new revert PR; it has to look the stop id up from the log's `Last note: escalation <stop id>` or the `## Escalations` section. Not a blocker, but the contract is implicit.
  SEVERITY: NIT
  ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 2
- TASK_GAP
  Requirement: "The escalation judge never archives itself; the chain archives it at the end of the project."
  Expected change site: workflow-templates/.clau
